thread:
maria: Heads up — PR #8721 is ready but I'm holding merge. This touches the routing/cache layer and we need alignment on the design in RFC-204 before we flip the flag. RFC: https://redwood.dev/rfcs/204 PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8721 Can arch take a quick look? I added a short canary plan in the PR description.

jonathan: Ran through the RFC briefly — main outstanding is TTL semantics for prefix cache. I left comments on both the RFC and PR. Short question: do we need per-model TTL or can we derive it from the seq_len histogram?

kai: Thanks @jonathan @maria. I think per-model TTL is safer for now. Also flagging perf regression concern if we keep KV eviction synchronous. Filed a tiny change in the PR to async eviction — PTAL.

maria: Good call. I pushed an update to the PR with a feature flag + unit test. Canary plan: 5% traffic on dedicated, ~10k requests/day, monitor latency and cache_hit_rate. If regressions <1% we proceed. Need architecture consensus before I enable.

arch-bot: RFC-204 status: REVIEW_REQUESTED. Reviewers assigned: @jonathan, @lee. Last updated 2044999000.

jonathan: I'll allocate time tomorrow morning to finish the RFC comments. If @lee or @kai can ack the async eviction approach that should unblock. Otherwise propose we gate merge on an explicit arch LGTM in the RFC thread.

kai: I'll add a short writeup in the RFC thread today describing invariants and fallback behavior. @maria, can you add a brief experiment metric list to the PR so SRE knows what to watch?

maria: Added metrics to the PR: latency_p50, latency_p95, cache_hit_rate, evictions_per_min, error_rate. Thanks — if we have an arch LGTM by EOD tomorrow I can schedule the canary for Wed morning.
